name: Tagsmith
description: Derives searchable, machine-readable tags (origin=, lang=, year= ...) from metadata Jellyfin already holds, and keeps them in sync as the library changes.
overview: Automatic namespaced metadata tags for Jellyfin.

versions.changelog:
## Breaking

- **Urdu now tags as Hindi.** On the next sync, every `lang=urdu` and `audio_lang=urdu` tag is rewritten to `hindi`; the Urdu collection's items merge into Hindi and the now-empty Urdu collection is deleted. Spoken dialogue either side of the border is Hindustani either way, and script only ever decided how subtitles were set, so the two are folded by default. To keep them separate, add both `lang:urdu => urdu` and `audio_lang:urdu => urdu` to the Aliases box — a bare `urdu => urdu` rule does not work, since a namespace-scoped rule always wins over a global one for the same value. If *Remove obsolete tags* is off, the fold adds `lang=hindi` without removing `lang=urdu`, leaving affected titles in both collections until a run with pruning enabled. Note also: any poster set by hand on the Urdu collection before this release is stored inside that collection's folder and is lost when the collection is deleted by the merge.
- **The artwork sets are replaced outright, not extended.** `origin/` is now a hand-made set covering all 206 countries at 1000x1500 (previously 7 machine-drawn flag posters at 400x600). `lang/` is replaced wholesale with a hand-made set covering 72 languages across 83 filenames at 1000x1500. Eight languages the old set covered have no poster in this release — Assamese, Bodo, Dogri, Kashmiri, Konkani, Manipuri, Sanskrit, Santali. Anyone who copied the previous artwork into `<config>/tagsmith/thumbnails/` should recopy it.

## Added

- `origin/` filenames are canonical tag-value slugs, verified against the plugin's own `CountryAliasCatalog` and `ThumbnailLocator`, so every country resolves to its own distinct poster. Three historical states — Czechoslovakia, the Soviet Union, and Yugoslavia — get their own posters and are deliberately not folded into any successor state.

## Internal

- Artwork now lives in the repository instead of being gitignored; the old `assets/placeholders/` solid-colour set is gone.
- `scripts/generate-artwork.mjs` is deleted — artwork is hand-maintained and there is no regeneration step for it any more. 17 of the 19 npm dev dependencies (the canvas/font/flag packages it used) go with it.
- `.gitattributes` now forces text diffing for `*.cs` files, because a literal NUL used as a delimiter in `TagAliasMap.cs` made git treat it as binary and hide the diff.
- Test suite grew from 391 to 408 tests, covering the new default alias behaviour, both opt-out rules, and the case where a global rule cannot override a scoped one.

## Compatibility

Targets Jellyfin server 10.11.11 (`targetAbi 10.11.11.0`), unchanged from the previous release.

# Tagsmith 0.2.1

## Breaking

**Some `lang=` and `origin=` values change, and every affected tag is rewritten on the next sync.** Nothing is lost — the old tag is replaced by the corrected one in the same pass — but two things are worth knowing. Any collection built from an old value is deleted and rebuilt under the new one, which means a poster you set by hand on, say, the old Spanish collection stays in the artwork folder under its old name and the new collection will not find it; rename the file to match. And any alias rule you wrote against an old value (`lang:spanish_castilian => spanish`, for instance) silently stops matching and can be deleted.

The changed values:

| Was | Now |
| --- | --- |
| `lang=spanish_castilian` | `lang=spanish` |
| `lang=dutch_flemish` | `lang=dutch` |
| `lang=romanian_moldavian_moldovan` | `lang=romanian` |
| `lang=chinese_traditional`, `lang=chinese_simplified` | `lang=chinese` |
| `lang=greek_modern_1453` | `lang=greek` |
| `origin=palestinian_territory` | `origin=palestine` |

…and around forty other languages with the same shape. `audio_lang=` values change the same way.

## Fixed

- **Languages were tagged with their scholarly names instead of the ones people use.** Jellyfin's language table answers with ISO 639-2 headings — "Spanish; Castilian", "Dutch; Flemish", "Chinese (Traditional)" — so Spanish tagged as `spanish_castilian`, which split one language across several tags, matched no artwork file, and is not what anyone would search for. Dialects, scripts and regional variants now fold to one value each: one Spanish collection rather than Spanish and Castilian, one Chinese rather than Traditional and Simplified, one Portuguese rather than Brazil and Portugal. Genuinely distinct languages are kept apart — North and South Ndebele stay two collections, and Ancient Greek is still not Greek.
- **"Palestinian Territory" did not resolve to Palestine.** The dictionary carried only the plural "Palestinian Territories", and the singular is what TMDb sends for a film, so those films sat in a collection of their own. The occupied and inverted ISO spellings are covered too.
- **The two Congos had no mapping at all.** "Democratic Republic of the Congo", "DR Congo", "DRC" and "Zaire" each tagged as themselves rather than joining `origin=congo_kinshasa`; "Republic of the Congo" likewise for `congo_brazzaville`. Bare "Congo" is still read as Congo-Brazzaville, which is what CLDR says and is genuinely ambiguous in English.

## Compatibility

Targets Jellyfin server **10.11.11**, unchanged from the previous release.

# Tagsmith 0.2.0

## Added

- **Three new browsable libraries, all off by default: Awards, Nominations and Curated Lists.**
  - Awards and nominations get one collection per ceremony *and* category — "Oscar – Best Picture" — rather than a single shelf per ceremony, since "everything that ever won an Oscar" is thousands of films and answers nothing. With all four ceremonies (Oscar, BAFTA, Golden Globe, Emmy) ticked that is around 80 collections in each of those two libraries, so the first sync after turning them on takes a while.
  - Nominations include the eventual winners, so the Nominations library is a superset of the Awards one rather than an alternative to it.
  - Curated Lists gets one collection per list you tick, up to seven: IMDb Top 250, the 2022 Sight & Sound critics' poll, AFI's 100 Years…100 Movies, BFI Top 100 British Films, the National Film Registry, The Criterion Collection, and the TSPDT 1000.
  - Library names default to Awards, Nominations and Curated Lists, and can be renamed on the settings page like the others.
- **Enabling a projection no longer builds an empty library by mistake.** Projecting a namespace is a separate switch from tagging it, and award, nomination and list tagging all default off — so ticking only "project award wins" would previously have created a library with nothing in it. Tagsmith now declines to build it and says why in the server log.

No artwork ships yet for the three new libraries, so their collections show the poster Jellyfin generates for them — a copy of the first film's poster — until you drop your own images into `<config>/tagsmith/thumbnails/award/`, `nomination/` and `list/`. A colon in the tag value becomes an underscore in the filename, so `award=oscar:best_picture` wants `oscar_best_picture.png`.

## Fixed

- **A projection that suddenly finds no tags at all no longer deletes every collection it built.** Untick every award ceremony, or have an embedded dataset fail to load, and that path previously removed a whole library's worth of collections. "No tags" is now treated as absence of evidence rather than as a decision to remove them. Collections for values that disappear one at a time are still cleaned up exactly as before.

## Compatibility

Targets Jellyfin server **10.11.11**, unchanged from the previous release.

This release adds new values to a saved setting. Downgrading to 0.1.1 or earlier after enabling any of the new projections may reset the plugin's settings to their defaults. Upgrading is unaffected.

# Tagsmith 0.1.1

## Fixed

- **The Languages and Decades collections libraries could come up empty and stay that way forever.** Jellyfin refuses to register a library folder that is empty at the moment it is created, and that is exactly the state Tagsmith's own projection folders started in — so anyone who turned those projections on in 0.1.0 got a library that appeared on the home screen but never listed a single collection, with nothing in the log to explain it. This is fixed, and any library already stuck empty populates itself on the next sync. There is no need to delete anything or recreate the library by hand.
- **Collection posters could get stuck on the wrong image and never pick up the one from the artwork folder.** Jellyfin quietly gives every new collection a poster copied from its first film, before Tagsmith has a chance to apply anything, and Tagsmith mistook that for a poster you had chosen and refused to overwrite it — so the artwork folder's poster could never reach a collection at all, even though it worked fine for the library tile. This is fixed, and any collection already stuck with the wrong poster is corrected on the next sync. A poster you genuinely set by hand is still never touched.

Posters you set by hand are still copied into the artwork folder so they survive a rebuild, but Jellyfin's auto-generated poster is no longer copied that way — previously that could overwrite a curated image file with a copy of one film's poster.

## Internal

- New tests cover the empty-library recovery and the server-generated-poster case in the artwork policy.

## Compatibility

Targets Jellyfin server **10.11.11**, unchanged from the previous release.

# Tagsmith 0.1.0

## Breaking

- **`lang=` now means the item's original language, not its audio tracks.** Previously `lang=` reflected whatever languages were found on the media files' audio streams; it now reflects what TMDb/TVDb say the film or show was actually made in. For example, a Hindi film with an English dub would previously have been tagged `lang=english` and is now tagged `lang=hindi`. Every `lang=` tag in your library is rewritten to the new value on the next sync, and the Languages collections/library are rebuilt to match. If you want the old audio-track behavior, turn on the new `audio_lang=` namespace in settings (off by default) — it keeps working exactly as `lang=` used to, including the same normalisation.

## Added

- `origin=` and `lang=` are now looked up from TMDb first, and from TVDb for TV shows when the official TheTVDB plugin is installed (a series matched only by a TVDb id is bridged through TMDb's find endpoint when possible). Jellyfin's own metadata is used only as a fallback when no external source knows the item. If a lookup fails outright — network trouble, a rate limit — rather than the item genuinely being unknown, Tagsmith leaves that item's existing origin/language tags alone instead of overwriting them with fallback values.
- New `award=` and `nomination=` namespaces (off by default), values like `award=oscar:best_picture`. Academy Award wins and nominations are covered completely since 1927/28; BAFTA, Golden Globe and Emmy coverage comes from Wikidata and is partial — winner-heavy and thinnest for acting/directing categories. Pick which ceremonies to tag individually on the settings page.
- New `list=` namespace (off by default) for membership in seven curated lists, each selectable on its own: IMDb Top 250, the 2022 Sight & Sound critics' poll, AFI's 100 Years...100 Movies, BFI Top 100 British films, the National Film Registry, The Criterion Collection, and the TSPDT 1000. These are snapshots taken when this release was built, not a live feed.
- A regular sync now fills in a poster on any collection or library that doesn't have one, and refreshes Tagsmith's own poster if the image file on disk changed — without ever touching a poster you set by hand. Previously this only happened for collections created in that same run, so anything older kept whatever poster it had, blank or not.
- New 16:9 library tile artwork (`thumbnails/<namespace>.png`) is shown on the Origins/Languages/Decades home-screen tiles, with a starter set included; a poster you set by hand on a library tile is now adopted the same way collection posters are.
- New "Delete projected collections" button in settings tears down every collection and library Tagsmith created (box sets and the Origins/Languages/Decades libraries) in one pass, with a confirmation dialog and dry-run support. Your media and tags are never touched, and any projection you leave enabled rebuilds on the next sync.
- The decade poster set (`thumbnails/year/`) is replaced with a curated, higher-resolution set.

## Fixed

- Language tags on TV series could come out completely empty, because the audio-track fallback checked the series item itself, which has no audio streams of its own (they live on the episodes). It now samples the first 32 episodes by premiere date.
- Several countries sent as bare ISO codes by TMDb/TVDb — including Russia, Nigeria, Angola, American Samoa, Burundi, Comoros and Saudi Arabia — were failing to tag at all because their code collided with a different country's display name in some locale.
- A blank tag namespace or separator could previously cause Tagsmith to claim, and delete, every tag in the library; this is now refused outright.
- Alias rules written against structured values like `oscar:best_picture` are now matched per segment, instead of being misread as targeting a whole namespace named after the ceremony.

## Internal

- First tests for `TagSynchronizer`'s sync lifecycle, plus new coverage for artwork policy, thumbnail lookup, curated-data loading, and alias rules.
- Award and list datasets are generated offline from third-party sources and embedded in the plugin (`THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md` documents licensing); the generators refuse to ship a dataset that collapsed well below its expected size.
- Artwork logic (hashing, applying, adopting, reapplying) is consolidated out of `CollectionProjector` into a new `ArtworkSynchronizer`.

## Compatibility

Targets Jellyfin server **10.11.11**, unchanged from the previous release.

## Tagsmith v0.0.6  ### Fixed  - **Collection artwork was never persisted.** Posters Tagsmith applied were written to disk but not to the library database, so they disappeared on restart.  ### Changed  - **A poster set on a collection is now saved to the thumbnails folder the moment you set it**, rather than on the next full sync. Previously it was lost if the collection was rebuilt before the sync ran. - **The nightly sync no longer touches artwork on existing collections.** It still applies the matching file to collections it creates, so a new country never appears as a blank tile.  ### Added  - **Reapply collection artwork** button on the settings page: pushes the thumbnails folder onto every projected collection, overriding posters set by hand. Use after dropping in a new set of images. - A plugin icon for the dashboard and catalogue.  **Compatibility:** Jellyfin 10.11.11. Unchanged since v0.0.2.

## Tagsmith v0.0.5

### Breaking

- **The collections projection did not work in 0.0.4 and is fixed here.** `ParentId` is ignored by Jellyfin 10.11.11, so every projected collection was created in your built-in Collections library while the Origins, Languages and Decades libraries stayed empty. Tagsmith now writes the box set folder into the projection's own directory. Collections stranded by 0.0.4 are detected and rewritten in the right place automatically on the first run — no manual cleanup.

### Fixed

- **Dry run no longer writes anything.** With a projection enabled, a dry run previously created libraries, created and deleted collections, wrote images and deleted files. It also no longer records managed prefixes: a prefix is a claim of ownership over every tag carrying it, so an abandoned experiment left Tagsmith deleting tags it had only been asked to describe.
- **A library you created yourself can no longer be adopted and then deleted.** Ownership was recorded by name, so an existing library called Origins was claimed, and turning the projection off with *remove collections when disabled* would destroy it along with all per-user access grants. Ownership is now recorded by item id, and a name held by something Tagsmith did not create is refused and logged.
- **Renaming a projection library in the dashboard no longer disables the projection.** A rename was indistinguishable from a deletion.
- **A metadata refresh can no longer overwrite your curated collection artwork.** Collections are created locked, and the applied image hash is tracked separately from the source file hash, so a provider-set poster is not mistaken for one you chose.
- **The first run created the library and no collections** — `AddVirtualFolder` was not awaited, so the library id was not yet registered when the collections were built.
- **A library name Jellyfin rewrites no longer spawns a new library every night.** Names containing characters Jellyfin strips never matched what it had created, producing Origins Countries, Origins Countries2, and so on.
- Orphaned box set folders are deleted rather than forgotten. The decision to abandon a projection is persisted immediately instead of at the end of a run that may be cancelled. The artwork namespace is contained inside the thumbnails directory. Duplicate collection records are collapsed.
- **A hand-edited config holding a movie's id would have deleted that movie file.** The delete path now resolves box sets only.

### Added

- A plugin icon for the dashboard sidebar and the plugin catalogue.

### Internal

- Release notes are passed to the workflow through the environment. Interpolated into the shell they were treated as command substitution, which is why the published 0.0.4 notes have every inline code span missing.
- New `BoxSetFolder`, `LibraryOwnership` and `MemberDiff` carry the logic that can be tested without a server. 175 tests, up from 95.

**Compatibility:** Jellyfin 10.11.11. Unchanged since v0.0.2.

## Tagsmith v0.0.4

### Breaking

- **Country tags in the  namespace will be rewritten on the first run after upgrading.** The new country canonicalisation is on by default. Every spelling of a country now resolves to one canonical English slug: , , , and  all become ;  becomes ;  becomes . If you had  or any other non-canonical form, it will be replaced. Turn off *Canonicalise country names* in the settings page to tag the raw metadata value instead and preserve the old behaviour.

- **Pruning now covers every prefix Tagsmith has ever written, not just currently active ones.** The plugin records all managed prefixes in a new  configuration list. Tags under a prefix that is no longer active — because you renamed a namespace or turned one off — are cleaned up on the next run rather than left behind. The list is visible and editable on the settings page: delete a line to make Tagsmith stop managing tags with that prefix permanently.

### Added

- **Collections projection: tag namespaces can now be browsed as a library of collections.** Enabling *Project origins*, *Project languages*, or *Project years* creates a Jellyfin library (named Origins, Languages, or Decades by default) whose collections are built from the tags. Every client can browse the collections without knowing tags exist. Tags remain the source of truth and collections are rebuilt from them on each run. Off by default.

- **Year tags project by decade rather than by individual year.**  stays precise as a tag, but the year projection groups items into , , and so on — ten tiles rather than a hundred.

- **Hand-set collection posters are adopted and preserved.** Set a poster on a collection in the Jellyfin UI and Tagsmith copies it into  as the stored artwork for that value, so it survives the collection being rebuilt. The folder also works in the other direction: drop a file there and it is applied to the matching collection. A hash guards both directions so a run with nothing changed writes nothing.

- **If a projection library is deleted in Jellyfin's own settings, Tagsmith treats that as intent and does not recreate it.** The corresponding projection is switched off in config automatically.

- **User alias rules.** A new *Aliases* field on the settings page accepts free-form rewrite rules applied after canonicalisation:  rewrites within one namespace,  applies everywhere, and an empty replacement drops the tag. Lines starting with  are comments. A malformed line is skipped rather than breaking a scan.

- **A starter set of collection artwork is published in  in the repository.** Flag posters for 7 origin countries, native-script language cards for 31 languages (English, French, Spanish, Chinese, Japanese, and all 22 languages of the Indian constitution's Eighth Schedule), and decade cards from the 1920s to the 2020s. Not bundled in the plugin; copy what you want into the thumbnails directory.

- **Historical states — Soviet Union, Yugoslavia, West Germany, Czechoslovakia — are deliberately not mapped by country canonicalisation.** They pass through as  and so on rather than being folded into successor states. Add an alias rule if you want different behaviour.

### Fixed

- **Renaming a namespace or changing the separator no longer leaves orphaned tags.** Previously, changing  to  would stop managing the old  tags; they would remain on every item indefinitely. The  mechanism ensures the old prefix is still pruned on subsequent runs.

### Internal

- Sub-task progress reporting now reserves the last 10% for the collection projection phase, rather than reaching 100% before projection starts.
- Elapsed time is logged separately for the tagging pass and the projection pass so performance can be measured.
- , , , and  are new;  registers  as a singleton.
- Claude agent definitions added for the commit-message, release-notes, test, and validate workflow steps.

**Compatibility:** Jellyfin 10.11.11 (). Unchanged since v0.0.2.
